## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Hybrid/unusual: the journal is overwhelmingly composed of INVITED papers (individuals directly invited to read a paper at the Society's fortnightly London meetings) which are NOT put through blind peer review and need not be anonymized. The only unsolicited submission category the journal reviews is 'Discussion Notes and Replies' (max 2000 words, must directly respond to a paper already published in the Proceedings or Supplementary Volume), which undergo blind refereeing with a separate anonymized cover sheet. |

> Source: https://academic.oup.com/aristotelian/pages/General_Instructions

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | No journal-specific AI policy page found for Proceedings of the Aristotelian Society (unlike some OUP journals, e.g. Journal of Pediatric Psychology, which have a dedicated /pages/ai-policy page — none exists at academic.oup.com/aristotelian). The journal therefore falls under Oxford University Press's general author-facing Gen AI policy: (1) AI tools (ChatGPT etc.) cannot be listed as authors; (2) any AI use to generate content/images, write code, process data, or translate MUST be disclosed in the cover letter and in the Methods/Acknowledgements section; (3) Gen AI must NOT be used for primary authorial tasks — generating arguments, philosophical analysis, or conclusions; permitted uses are narrow (grammar/spelling checks, alt-text, reference checking, abstract/keyword generation); (4) authors remain fully accountable for accuracy/originality. This is OUP's blanket policy, not verified as journal-customized for the Proceedings. |
| **Source URL** | https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/publishing-policies/author-use-of-artificial-intelligence |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** For all practical purposes the journal does NOT accept unsolicited full-length article submissions — main papers are commissioned via direct invitation to read at the Society's fortnightly meetings and are later published in the Proceedings. The only route open to outside authors without invitation is a short (<=2000 word) Discussion Note or Reply that directly engages a paper already published in the Proceedings or the Supplementary Volume.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic philosophy across broad traditions (epistemology, philosophy of mind, metaphysics, meta-ethics), history of Western philosophy (incl. Hegel, Malebranche, Nietzsche, Iris Murdoch, Stoicism), cross-traditional/comparative philosophy (e.g. Kumārila Bhaṭṭa/Sanskrit philosophy of language featured in Vol.126 Iss.1), critical theory and social/political philosophy, short critical discussion notes responding to a specific published paper
